slices.name: ws01-28-brand-marks
slices.brief:
WS01 slice 28 of 32 (checkpoint D, the design system; slices 20 to 32; its draft PR is #108). Branch redesign/ws01-design-system, HEAD df62ca3 (slice 27); the base for diffs is df62ca3. Checkpoints A, B and C are merged to main and live. Read first: REDESIGN_STATUS.md (Ordering rules, lines 7 to 11; the acceptance table with its AC10 row (line 34, still Planned: this slice fills it), its AC5 row (line 29), AC6 row (line 30), AC14 row (line 38) and T2 row (line 58) as the pattern for a filled row, and its AC8 row (line 32, which this slice leaves alone unless the fixture page's boxes change); the step 27 block (lines 730 to 770) and the step 26 block (lines 688 to 728, with the StatusBadge paragraph at 697 to 703, the LCA tag at 699 and the judgement call at 716); Decisions (Appearance control and the rook mark (steps 21 and 28), line 966, which this slice makes true; the White and Black markers from step 27, line 968, only as a pattern for a planned line marked done); Deviations (Step 26, lines 1100 to 1110, whose sentence at 1104 says the LCA tag has no mark until step 28; Step 27, lines 1111 to 1122, as the pattern); Verify items (the step 27 ones, lines 1299 to 1316, as the pattern); Follow-ups (The LCA tag's rook from step 26, line 1459; K reviews the step 27 judgement calls, line 1463; The baseline sampler waits for content from step 27, line 1468; Classes only docs and tests name reach the CSS from step 23, line 1425; The a11y servers share one database from step 23, line 1431); these line numbers were measured on the tree that holds slice 27 finished), docs/redesign/REDESIGN_SPEC.md (the logo row of section 1.1, line 138; acceptance criterion 10, line 357; the new files, lines 305, 337 and 342, the last naming Seal, which step 31 builds from LcaMark; the header, lines 390 to 392, the footer, line 395, and the identity band, line 401; WS12's digital card, line 1698; WS14's changes to the governance pages, line 1884; Decision D1, line 2014; the WS01 deviations list, line 112, which carries step 26's and step 27's sentences), docs/redesign/DESIGN_REPLAN_phase0.md (lines 174 to 176 and 904 to 908, how K's header note was read; lines 926 and 937: Q9 settled with no cream plate and D1 amended), the decided boards docs/redesign/decided-boards/Nav-Header-Final.dc.html (the rook at line 51, .nf-rook: 30px, filled #ffffff, and the brand link's markup), Nav-Mobile-Final.dc.html (line 58, .mf-mark: 28px in the phone app bar) and Nav-Footer-Final.dc.html (the 44px cream plate at lines 49 to 51, note 1 at line 180, Q9 at line 196, the app bar's mark at line 139), the option board docs/redesign/lca-redesign-boards/boards/Looks-3-Minimal-Tile.dc.html (the LCA tag with its rook at line 329; the mark is 11px and fills with the tag's words colour, line 93) and docs/redesign/lca-redesign-boards/kit.css (.k-mark, line 133, and .k-brand, lines 139 to 142), src/components/layout/Navbar.tsx (lines 1 to 20 and 205 to 320), src/components/layout/Footer.tsx (all 125 lines), src/pages/AboutPage.tsx (all 43), src/areas/governance/components/GovLayout.tsx (lines 86 to 104: what draws the page's heading; not changed), src/components/PageHero.tsx (draws no logo or mark), src/components/StatusBadge.tsx (all 230 lines, especially 1 to 30, 56 to 70, 95 to 150), public/favicon.svg, index.html (lines 5 and 24), src/assets/lca-logo.webp (look at it), the module declarations for image imports in src, src/lib/features.ts, src/lib/brand.ts, src/index.css (the brand colours at 35 to 38, the gold tokens at 237 to 239 and the surface tokens at 227 to 233, 398 to 404, 459 to 465, 504 to 510, 553 to 559 and 604 to 610), the tests that sit around this work: test/unit/goldText.test.ts (lines 742, 826 to 832, 1081 and 1115 to 1120: the pinned lines of StatusBadge.tsx and the footer's heading), test/unit/contrast.test.ts (lines 395 to 415, 698 to 728 and 1144), test/unit/raw-colours.test.ts with test/unit/fixtures/raw-colours-allowlist.json (the entries for Navbar.tsx, Footer.tsx, AboutPage.tsx and StatusBadge.tsx), test/unit/semantic-map-grounds.test.ts (lines 330 to 340, the white mats), test/unit/status-badge.test.tsx (lines 120 to 160), test/unit/status-badge-edges.test.tsx (lines 105 to 190), test/unit/appearance-control.test.tsx and appearance-control-off.test.tsx (both draw the Footer), test/unit/news-pinned-flag.test.tsx (lines 15 to 29, a switch flipped inside one file), test/unit/status-dot-newlook.test.tsx (the mock of src/lib/features), test/unit/base-components-types.test.ts (how it compiles what a caller may write), test/unit/browser-test-wiring.test.ts (the file list and the dash check at lines 455 to 495), test/unit/redesign-status-step27.test.ts (all of it: the date line at 103 to 105, the follow-up counts at 303 to 312, the deviation at 55 and 163 to 176 and the spec sentence at 327 to 346) with the earlier record tests, and the browser harness (playwright.config.ts, test/a11y/support.ts, baseline.ts, baseline.json, components.spec.ts as the pattern for a spec that runs the accessibility checker on both builds, components-edges.spec.ts lines 200 to 225 where every status mark is probed, tokens.spec.ts line 321, dark-grounds.spec.ts, known-violations.json) so the flag-off baseline comparison stays green. The lead's notes win over this brief and the manifest where they differ (they say nothing on this slice beyond the standing rules and one note for step 32 on the baseline sampler, which this slice must not break: difference 9): <scratchpad>/ws01-lead-notes.md. The manifest entry (order 28) is in <scratchpad>/ws01-manifest.json. node_modules is installed; nothing ever runs against a remote database or the Cloudflare account; agents never commit, stash, reset or check out anything; the working tree is the only copy. Environment facts for this container: the pinned Playwright expects a Chromium build the container does not have, so every npm run test:a11y here runs as PW_CHROMIUM_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium npm run test:a11y (the config reads that variable); never run playwright install; WRANGLER_SEND_METRICS=false on every wrangler command; localhost is exempt from the outbound proxy, so the a11y servers on 127.0.0.1 work. Dependencies are exact-pinned (no caret) at versions at least two weeks old, with package-lock.json updated by npm install; this slice needs no new package. The branch tip is df62ca3 (slice 27), and the working tree is clean when the slice starts; origin/redesign/ws01-design-system carried a12c74e (slice 26) when this was measured and carries later commits only once the lead pushes, and the local main ref is 4c1a466 and does not carry the checkpoint merges, so a diff against the local main shows far more than this slice: take this slice's own changes as the working tree against df62ca3. Build exactly this. Logo and mark components, placed where they exist today. src/components/LcaMark.tsx is the one-colour rook-Louisiana mark as inline SVG, reusing the single path from public/favicon.svg (viewBox 0 0 100 100). It uses fill currentColor and a title prop (default "Louisiana Chess Association"), and is for the header at every width and tight spaces (D1). src/components/LcaLogo.tsx wraps src/assets/lca-logo.webp, the file Navbar and Footer use today. It renders width, height and alt, has no colour, filter or className-colour props, and is set on white or cream; the official logo is never recoloured.

Under newLook: the current Navbar shows LcaMark at every width, the Footer keeps LcaLogo, and AboutPage shows LcaLogo on a white or cream mat near its heading, because D1 gives the full-colour logo to About and history pages. With the flag off, all three render as today. Slice 31 keeps the AboutPage placement inside the heritage layout. ChampionsPage, the other history page, is recorded with the remaining D1 placements that do not exist yet (the homepage identity band, the membership card, certificates and the print kit cover) in REDESIGN_STATUS.md for WS03, WS10 and WS12. Log a follow-up to point AdminEmailPage's preview LOGO_URL at /email-logo.jpg instead of the 2.4 MB public/lca-logo.jpg. Only the new look changes what a visitor sees. With newLook off, Navbar, Footer and AboutPage render the markup they render today, to the attribute: unlike step 27 there is no ungated difference to allow, and the three files may import the switch and the new components but draw them only under it (the old img elements stay in the flag-off branch, not LcaLogo, whose markup is not the same). The LCA tag's rook (difference 4) is the one change that does not depend on the switch, because the status path of StatusBadge is the new path, drawn by no page (the fixture page, which exists only in the accessibility test build, is its one caller) and never read the switch; say so in the record. Nothing under public/, functions/, workers/ or index.html changes, and nothing in AdminEmailPage.tsx: the follow-up the brief asks for is a record, not a change. git diff against df62ca3 shows changes under src only in LcaMark.tsx, LcaLogo.tsx, Navbar.tsx, Footer.tsx, AboutPage.tsx and StatusBadge.tsx. Verify items from the manifest, each to be re-checked against the tree as it is now (the earlier finding follows): Which logo file is current. (src/assets/lca-logo.webp (400 x 399, 16 KB) is imported by Navbar.tsx and Footer.tsx and is the current site logo. public/lca-logo.jpg (4355 x 4340, 2.4 MB) is used only as LOGO_URL in AdminEmailPage.tsx:45 for the email preview; real emails use public/email-logo.jpg (280 px) via functions/utils/emailLayout.ts and site.ts. LcaLogo wraps the webp; the jpg is a source master. Re-checked: the sizes hold: lca-logo.webp is 400 x 399 and 16,468 bytes, lca-logo.jpg is 4,355 x 4,340 and 2,403,503 bytes, email-logo.jpg is 280 x 279 and 18,914 bytes. The webp is imported at Navbar.tsx line 10 and Footer.tsx line 5 and drawn at Navbar.tsx line 230 and Footer.tsx lines 58 to 62; the jpg is declared at AdminEmailPage.tsx line 45 and drawn at line 65, 120px wide; the email template draws email-logo.jpg 140px wide at emailLayout.ts line 164, and site.ts's emailLogoUrl (line 45) has no caller outside test/unit/site-url.test.ts, so the claim about site.ts holds only as a helper nobody calls. Two things the finding leaves out: the webp is a lossy file with no alpha channel and all four corners and the top edge read #ffffff, so it carries its own white ground and is set on white wherever it is drawn, whatever the page ground is; and public/ ships whole, so dist/ carries the 2.4 MB jpg beside dist/assets, which this slice does not change.) Rook mark source. (public/favicon.svg is a single path with a navy fill #1a2744 and a dark-scheme gold fill #ffd54a. Re-checked: it is 420 bytes with viewBox 0 0 100 100, one path of 196 characters starting M5 7.1H16.6V23H28.3 and ending V7.1Z, a title element and a style block; the fill is not an attribute but a CSS class on the path, .mark{fill:#1a2744} with .mark{fill:#ffd54a} under a dark device, so LcaMark copies the path's d and none of the file's colours, and #ffd54a is in no site token (the site's gold on a dark ground is #c8a94a). The path is byte for byte the one every board draws as .k-mark (checked against Nav-Header.dc.html), and index.html line 5 links the file as the site icon, which is already the rook, so the favicon needs no work.) D1 placements in WS01 scope. (D1 gives the full-colour logo to About and history pages; /about exists today and is placed here, the rest are deferred. Re-checked against D1's own text (spec line 2014): it lists more than the finding does, see difference 5. /about exists (App.tsx line 101) and is one of six heritage pages (src/lib/themeScopes.ts lines 43 to 50), but is drawn in the base look on both builds until step 31, since nothing in src/App.tsx reads the route-to-look map yet and ThemeScope is drawn by the fixture page alone.) Further differences between the manifest's assumptions and the tree, all measured at the tree this slice starts from (slice 27 finished). (1) The header already shows its brand at every width, so the swap replaces one element and no width rule has to be built. Navbar.tsx draws the logo as an img (line 230: the import at line 10, h-11 w-11 rounded-lg object-contain, 44px, so a white square on the navy) and the two-line name as text (lines 232 to 235, Louisiana Chess over Association), both inside the brand Link (229), in one h-16 (64px) bar that is bg-brand-navy in every look (227 and 228); no class hides either at any width. The squeeze, the aria-label on the brand link and the one-row condensing rule are WS02's (spec lines 390 to 392) and are not built here. Under newLook replace the img only: keep the Link, the name and the bar as they are. The decided boards draw the mark white (#ffffff) on the navy, 30px in the desktop and tablet bar (Nav-Header-Final line 51) and 28px in the phone app bar (Nav-Mobile-Final line 58); the header stays navy in dark mode and in every look, so the mark takes text-white (white on #1a2744 reads 14.81:1, and a graphic needs 3:1, WCAG 1.4.11), a class that adds no raw colour, and the sizes come from the boards. Today the brand link's name is read twice, once from the img's alt and once from the words beside it; under newLook the mark beside the words is decorative, hidden from screen readers, so the link is named once, by its words. Record the choice of size and colour as a judgement call. (2) The footer draws the logo straight on the navy with no plate, and the file's own white ground is what satisfies 'set on white or cream'. Footer.tsx imports the file at line 5 and draws it at lines 58 to 62 (an img, h-14 w-14 rounded-xl object-contain, 56px) inside the brand block, on the navy band, where the file's white square shows as it does in the header today. The decided Nav-Footer-Final board draws a 44px cream plate (#fbfaf6, a colour no token or file under src has) with the words 'official logo' as a stand-in, but K settled Q9 for the header as no plate (DESIGN_REPLAN_phase0.md lines 904 and 926) and the brief's footer line (spec line 395) says the brand block keeps the official logo; the option board Nav-Footer draws the rook in gold at 44px in the brand block instead, which the brief overrules. So draw LcaLogo at 56px with no plate and no ground of its own, and record the plate as a judgement call for K's eye (Q9's footer half, which the header ruling did not settle in words). Footer.tsx line 94 is pinned (difference 8): the five lines of the img (58 to 62) must stay five lines in the newLook branch, or the pin moves in the same change. Under newLook the footer's name text sits beside the logo, whose file already spells the name; decide whether the logo's alt is the name or empty there (the words beside it say it), keep the choice in one place and record it. (3) About has no heading of its own above the fold, and no mat. AboutPage.tsx (43 lines) draws its content inside GovLayout (line 9), whose PageHero draws the page's h1 ('About LCA' over 'The Louisiana Chess Association'); GovLayout is not in this slice's files and serves three other governance pages, so leave it alone and put the logo in AboutPage's own markup, beside or above the 'Who we are' block (line 12, its first h2), at a width a 390px screen holds with no sideways scroll. The page has no mat today, and a white ground is not free to add: raw-colours.test.ts and semantic-map-grounds.test.ts fail on a bg-white that no keep entry names, and the five existing white mats (four club logos and the sign-in QR code's quiet zone) are keep entries in scripts/codemods/semantic-colours.map.json whose counts are pinned. The logo's file is already white edge to edge (the first verify item above), so the mat is a frame around it: padding and a border in tokens, on bg-surface (white in the base look, #fffdf8 in heritage, so cream where step 31 draws it, and the dark surface in dark mode, where the file's own white square still carries the white), with no bg-white. If the build finds a white ground is needed after all, add a sixth keep entry with its reason and move the pinned counts, and say so. Mark the frame with data-slot="lca-logo-mat", since the manifest says step 31 keeps this placement inside the heritage layout, and step 31's brief calls it the logo on its white or cream mat. Do not touch the page's navy Get involved box or its text. (4) The manifest's file list leaves out StatusBadge.tsx, but the record promises the LCA tag's rook to this step in four places: the step 26 block (lines 699 and 716), Deviations step 26 (line 1104: 'The LCA tag has no mark until step 28's LcaMark, where the tile draws the rook'), the follow-up 'The LCA tag's rook (step 26)' (line 1459: 'step 28 adds it through LcaMark') and a comment in test/unit/status-badge.test.tsx line 137; and D1 gives the rook to small badges. The tag is the LCA status tag of StatusBadge's status path (STATUS_CLASSES line 66), drawn today with its words only: StatusBadge line 141 skips the mark for partner and lca, and the tests say so (status-badge.test.tsx 133 to 140 expects no mark for lca, status-badge-edges.test.tsx 108 to 120 expects every child of a tag to be a status-mark, and components-edges.spec.ts 207 to 225 probes every [data-slot="status-mark"] and counts at least 7 turned marks besides the live ones). The tile (Looks-3-Minimal-Tile line 329) draws the rook before the words, 11px, filled with the words' colour, hidden from screen readers. Build it: draw LcaMark in the LCA tag before its words, decorative, in the tag's words colour, with no colour of its own, and move the pins that say the tag has none, keeping every other status's mark and the live dot's static animation exactly as they are. Keep what the gold guard and the contrast test pin in place: the tone strings on lines 26 to 41 (the gold guard names line 28, goldText.test.ts 742 and 1081) and the eight status strings on lines 59 to 66 (contrast.test.ts 717 to 724) must stay on those lines, so shorten the file's header comment by one line to make room for the import, as step 26 did, or move the pins in the same change. The fixture page is not changed: it draws the LCA tag already, and its 13 [data-status] elements, five Buttons and boxes stay as they are (the tag grows by the mark and its gap, which the scope-switch specs measure as no move on a switch). Add StatusBadge.tsx and the tests you move to the record's Files and to its list of files beyond the step's list. (5) D1's placements, as the tree has them. D1 (spec line 2014, the logo row at line 138, acceptance criterion 10 at line 357) gives the rook to the header, the favicon, small badges, QR centres and social avatars, and the official logo to the footer brand block, the homepage identity band, the About and history pages, emails, the print kit, certificates and the membership card. Measured: header, this slice; favicon, already the rook and unchanged; small badges, the LCA tag (difference 4); QR centres, none (the only QR is the two-step sign-in code, markup the sign-in provider returns, AccountSecurityPage.tsx lines 220 to 221, which a phone must read, so no mark goes in it); social avatars, none in the code. Logo: footer and About, this slice; emails, drawn today (emailLayout.ts line 164, email-logo.jpg on navy) and unchanged; the share card, public/og-default.jpg (1200 by 630, the full-colour logo on a white rounded plate over a darkened photo), used at index.html line 24 and as the fallback at functions/utils/events/linkPreview.ts line 66, and unchanged. Not in the tree: the homepage identity band (WS03, spec line 401), the membership card (WS12's digital card, spec line 1698), certificates and the print kit cover (the brief names no workstream for either: record them as without an owner and ask K to place them), and the Champions page, which exists (src/pages/ChampionsPage.tsx, WS10's). The heritage pages the brief changes are six (themeScopes.ts lines 43 to 50: About, Board, Bylaws, Minutes, Annual meeting and Champions), and the manifest places About and records Champions only: record Board, Bylaws, Minutes and Annual meeting as well (all four exist today, and WS14 changes them, spec line 1884), leaving it to K whether D1's history pages include them. Record all of these with their owners under the step's follow-ups, as the manifest asks, in one follow-up headed (step 28). (6) The image files, measured. There are 14: five under public (email-logo.jpg 18,914 bytes, favicon.svg 420, icons.svg 5,031, lca-logo.jpg 2,403,503, og-default.jpg 103,886) and nine under src/assets (five slide pictures, lca-logo.webp 16,468, hero.png, react.svg and vite.svg). Four carry the full-colour logo (the webp, the large jpg, email-logo.jpg and og-default.jpg), one is the rook (favicon.svg), and four are referenced by nothing at all (hero.png, which step 29 leaves out of the image pipeline, react.svg, vite.svg and icons.svg, leftovers the audit board lists and not this slice's). The logo is drawn at 3 img elements in 3 files (Navbar.tsx 230, Footer.tsx 58, AdminEmailPage.tsx 65), the rook by none, and no component named LcaMark, LcaLogo or Seal exists. There is no apple-touch icon, no web manifest and no other social image. The 13 inline svg elements under src (FacebookIcon 1, ResultCell 1, StatusBadge 6, GovLayout 2, ClubLocationPicker 1, LCAMap 2) are icons and status marks, none of them a brand mark. The one build asset the logo adds is the hashed webp the two imports already emit, so dist/assets keeps its 127 files. (7) The follow-up the manifest asks for, and what it leaves out. AdminEmailPage.tsx declares LOGO_URL = '/lca-logo.jpg' at line 45 and draws it 120px wide at line 65 in the email preview, which is the one use of the 2.4 MB file; the real email draws email-logo.jpg (280 pixels, 18,914 bytes) 140px wide, so the smaller file serves the preview at the density it needs. Log the follow-up (a small fix for whoever next changes the admin email screen, WS08's admin work, and a question for K whether public/lca-logo.jpg stays as the source master or leaves the deployed files), and leave the page alone. The preview's comment at lines 41 to 44 says the relative path is right wherever the site is deployed, which is also true of /email-logo.jpg. (8) Pins the new code meets. test/unit/goldText.test.ts lines 1115 to 1120 holds the footer's heading at Footer.tsx:94 (tracking-widest text-lca-gold) and lines 742 and 1081 hold StatusBadge.tsx:28, so nothing before those lines may add or lose a line, or the pins move in the same change. test/unit/raw-colours.test.ts and its allowlist hold the white veils and hover colours by file and class (Navbar.tsx four entries, 12 uses: bg-white/5 twice, hover:bg-white/10 eight times, hover:bg-white/15 once, hover:text-[#1877F2] once; Footer.tsx three entries; AboutPage.tsx one; StatusBadge.tsx one; 35 entries and 49 uses in all), so a class string written in both branches of a ternary moves a count: write each such class once. test/unit/contrast.test.ts lines 395 to 415 reads the files the six heritage pages load, which will now include LcaLogo.tsx, and 698 to 728 holds every text-status class, by line, beside its tint. test/unit/appearance-control.test.tsx and appearance-control-off.test.tsx draw the Footer with newLook on and off, so they draw the new branch. No unit test draws Navbar or AboutPage today and none names the logo (a search of test for logo, rook, alt= and the two file names finds only planted strings in the codemod tests and the two server tests that read email-logo.jpg), so the flag-off test holds today's markup of the three as literal strings copied from the files before you edit them, in a fixture beside the test, and the flag is flipped inside one test file with the hoisted getter of test/unit/news-pinned-flag.test.tsx (lines 15 to 29), which draws both ways and compares. The Navbar needs the auth context and the database client mocked, as other tests do (test/unit/reminder-bell.test.tsx); the image import resolves in the test environment already (the two appearance tests draw the Footer). LcaMark.tsx and LcaLogo.tsx export components and types only, because the linter's only-export-components rule is an error here: any constant stays unexported, and step 31's Seal takes the mark by drawing LcaMark inside its own svg rather than by importing a path. There is no snapshot anywhere in test. (9) The baseline and the step 32 note. test/a11y/baseline.ts samples the page body and, inside main, the first Button, the first th and the first .font-mono on /, /tournaments, /membership and /tournaments/fx-t-done. The header and the footer sit outside main and paint the same background and colours either way, and nothing here adds a th or a font-mono element or touches TournamentDetailPage.tsx, so the baseline cannot move provided Navbar.tsx and Footer.tsx draw the same pixels with newLook off. The lead's note for step 32 (the last section of the lead's notes) records that the accessibility job failed once on a74f221 and passed on a rerun: baseline.ts sampled /tournaments/fx-t-done after the local database answered 'database is locked' to the page's data request, so the page drew its error text (the first Button a plain outline button, no table header, no monospace element) and the comparison read a colour change. Step 32 owns the fix; this slice must not take it on and must not break the sampler: leave baseline.ts and baseline.json alone, add no request to that page, and make the spec you write wait for the content it reads (the header's brand link, the footer, the page's heading), not for network idle alone. If baseline.ts fails with that signature (the page drawing its error, a lock in a server's log) and no colour or font difference, rerun the whole run once, quote both runs, and never rewrite baseline.json; a failure with a real colour or font difference is a defect in the slice. Steps 26 and 27 met the same lock (follow-up 'The a11y servers share one database (step 23)', line 1431). (10) The browser harness and the first checker run on /about. No spec reads the header's or the footer's image today (tokens.spec.ts line 321 reads the footer's background only), dark-grounds.spec.ts scans every element on /, /tournaments and /membership on a11y-on for a navy glyph below its ratio and an opaque white ground that is not a mat behind an image (a white mark on the navy and an svg with no ground pass both), and no spec visits /about, so the accessibility checker has never run there: its first run is this slice's. A finding outside the logo (in the page's text or the navy box, say) is recorded, and fixed if it is token-level or under newLook; nothing goes in known-violations.json. The new spec, test/a11y/brand.spec.ts, runs on both builds and skips per build the tests of the build it does not check: on a11y-on, at 1280, 768 and 390 pixels, the header holds one [data-slot="lca-mark"] and no img, whose one path's d is the favicon's (read from public/favicon.svg in the test, so the two cannot drift), whose computed fill is white and reaches 3:1 on the header's computed background, also with a dark device; the brand link is named once, 'Louisiana Chess Association'; the page does not scroll sideways at 390; the footer's [data-slot="lca-logo"] img is 400 by 399 naturally and the bytes the page fetches for it equal src/assets/lca-logo.webp on disk (16,468 bytes, same hash) with computed filter none, opacity 1 and mix-blend-mode normal; /about shows the same logo in its mat at 390 and 1280 with the same file; the LCA tag on the base fixture draws its rook, hidden from screen readers, in the tag's words colour; and the checker (the WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 A and AA rules, as components.spec.ts runs it) finds nothing in the header and the footer and on /about at 1280 and 390. On a11y-off: the header's img is today's (the hashed webp, its alt, a 44 by 44 box), no mark is drawn, the footer's img is 56 by 56, /about draws no logo and no mat, and the checker's findings on /about and the footer are recorded as measured (a finding on a11y-off outside this slice's files is recorded, and the same rule applies: nothing in known-violations.json). The spec is the only browser change except for the pins difference 4 moves. (11) Names. LcaMark takes a title (default 'Louisiana Chess Association'): given words it is an image with its title as its name (an svg with role img and a title element, which the checker accepts; an aria-label on a bare svg with no role is not allowed), and given an empty string it is decorative (no title element, hidden from screen readers), which is how the header and the LCA tag draw it, since words beside it name the place.
